description: Real-world scenario benchmark for testing live proactive agent. Each scenario defines a situation where ambient recommendations would be genuinely useful. Designed for role-play testing with the live agent.

scenarios.title: Sprint standup — blocked task you forgot to mention
scenarios.setup: You're in a daily standup. You mentioned what you did yesterday but forgot to mention you're blocked on a dependency from another team. The conversation is moving to the next person.
script_outline: P1 (you): Yesterday I finished the auth migration and started on the dashboard refactor.
P2: Cool, anything blocking you?
P1: Uh, no I think I'm good. [PAUSE — agent should trigger here]
P2: Alright, P3 your turn.
scenarios.expected_trigger_moment: When P1 says 'no I think I'm good' — the agent knows from prior context that the dashboard refactor needs the API team's schema changes
scenarios.notes: Tests whether the agent can catch omissions the wearer might forget under time pressure

scenarios.title: Behavioral interview — STAR method gap
scenarios.setup: You're being interviewed and asked 'Tell me about a time you dealt with conflict.' You start telling the story but skip the Result part of STAR.
script_outline: P2 (interviewer): Tell me about a time you had to deal with a difficult team conflict.

P1 (you): Sure, so at my last company we had a disagreement about the architecture. The backend team wanted microservices but frontend wanted a monolith. I set up a meeting and we mapped out the trade-offs on a whiteboard. We ended up going with a hybrid approach.
[PAUSE — agent should trigger: you didn't state the RESULT/impact]
scenarios.expected_trigger_moment: After P1 finishes the story without quantifying the outcome
scenarios.notes: Agent should suggest adding the result: timeline improvement, team satisfaction, etc.

scenarios.title: Salary negotiation — anchoring opportunity
scenarios.setup: You're negotiating a job offer. The recruiter just named a number that's below market. You're about to respond.
script_outline: P2 (recruiter): Based on your experience, we're thinking $130K base with standard benefits.
P1 (you): Hmm okay, that's... [PAUSE — agent should trigger before you respond]
scenarios.expected_trigger_moment: Right when P1 hesitates — before they accidentally anchor low
scenarios.notes: Agent should surface market data context and suggest counter-anchoring technique

scenarios.title: Dinner party — dietary restriction someone mentioned earlier
scenarios.setup: You're hosting dinner. Earlier a guest mentioned they're vegetarian but now you're about to suggest ordering from a steakhouse.
script_outline: P1 (you): Okay so for dinner I was thinking we could order from that new steakhouse on—
[AGENT should trigger: P3 mentioned being vegetarian 10 minutes ago]
scenarios.expected_trigger_moment: When P1 starts suggesting the steakhouse
scenarios.notes: Tests long-context recall — the agent heard the dietary mention earlier in the buffer

scenarios.title: Client call — promising a deadline you can't meet
scenarios.setup: You're on a call with a client who asks when a feature will ship. You're about to say 'two weeks' but your team's sprint is already full.
script_outline: P2 (client): So when can we expect the analytics dashboard to be ready?
P1 (you): I think we can probably get that to you in about two weeks—
[AGENT should trigger: you're overcommitting]
scenarios.expected_trigger_moment: When P1 starts committing to a timeline
scenarios.notes: Tests whether agent catches overcommitment. In real use, agent would have calendar/project context.

scenarios.title: Thesis defense — committee question you're dodging
scenarios.setup: A committee member asks about a limitation of your methodology. You start answering but drift to a different topic.
script_outline: P2 (professor): How do you account for selection bias in your participant sample?
P1 (you): Great question. So our participants were recruited through university channels and we had a diverse age range from 18 to 45. The study design was validated by...
[AGENT should trigger: you didn't actually address selection bias]
scenarios.expected_trigger_moment: When P1 pivots away from the actual question

scenarios.title: Doctor visit — forgot to mention a symptom
scenarios.setup: You're at the doctor describing headaches but forgot to mention the dizziness that's been happening too. The doctor is about to wrap up.
script_outline: P1 (you): Yeah the headaches have been happening for about two weeks, mostly in the morning.
P2 (doctor): Okay, that sounds like it could be tension headaches. I'll prescribe some—
[AGENT should trigger: you also mentioned dizziness to someone last week]
scenarios.expected_trigger_moment: When the doctor starts concluding without P1 mentioning the dizziness
scenarios.notes: High-stakes omission. Agent needs to catch that the wearer is forgetting to mention something important.

scenarios.title: Brainstorm — idea getting steamrolled
scenarios.setup: You proposed an idea 3 minutes ago that got ignored. Someone else just proposed something similar and is getting praise.
script_outline: P1 (you): [3 minutes ago] What if we used a queue-based system to handle the spikes?
P3: Hmm I don't know...
P2: [now] I think we should implement a message queue to manage traffic bursts.
P3: Oh that's brilliant, yeah let's do that.
[AGENT should trigger: P2 just restated your idea]
scenarios.expected_trigger_moment: When P3 praises P2's idea that matches P1's earlier suggestion
scenarios.notes: Tests social awareness — detecting when the wearer's contribution was co-opted

scenarios.title: Product demo — prospect dropped a buying signal
scenarios.setup: You're demoing your product. The prospect just said 'We've been looking for exactly this' but you kept demoing features instead of closing.
script_outline: P2 (prospect): Honestly this is exactly what we've been looking for. Our current tool doesn't do half of this.
P1 (you): Great! So let me also show you the reporting module, it has these charts—
[AGENT should trigger: stop demoing, start closing]
scenarios.expected_trigger_moment: When P1 continues demoing after a clear buying signal
scenarios.notes: Tests detecting buying/commitment signals and recommending a strategic pivot

scenarios.title: 1:1 with report — they're about to escalate emotionally
scenarios.setup: You're giving feedback to a direct report. Their tone is getting defensive and you're about to push harder on the point.
script_outline: P1 (you/manager): The last two deliverables had significant quality issues and it's impacting the team.
P2 (report): I mean, I've been working 60 hour weeks and nobody seems to notice that.
P1: Well the hours don't matter if the output—
[AGENT should trigger: de-escalation needed]
scenarios.expected_trigger_moment: When P1 starts dismissing P2's emotional response
scenarios.notes: Tests emotional intelligence — agent should recommend acknowledging the effort before continuing the feedback

scenarios.title: Study group — fundamental misconception going uncorrected
scenarios.setup: You're in a study group. Someone just explained a concept incorrectly and others are nodding along. You noticed the error but the conversation moved on.
script_outline: P2: So basically in TCP, the three-way handshake is SYN, ACK, FIN.
P3: Right, that makes sense.
P2: And then the connection is established.
[AGENT should trigger: it's SYN, SYN-ACK, ACK — not SYN, ACK, FIN]
scenarios.expected_trigger_moment: When the incorrect explanation is accepted by the group
scenarios.notes: Tests factual correction in educational context

scenarios.title: Conference networking — missed connection opportunity
scenarios.setup: Someone at a conference just mentioned they work on a project related to your research. You're about to end the conversation with a generic 'nice to meet you.'
script_outline: P2: Yeah so I've been working on egocentric video understanding at Meta FAIR.
P1 (you): Oh that's cool. Well it was nice meeting you—
[AGENT should trigger: this person's work is directly relevant to your thesis]
scenarios.expected_trigger_moment: When P1 starts wrapping up without recognizing the connection
scenarios.notes: Tests recognizing relevance to wearer's known interests/work

testing_instructions.how_to_test: Role-play each scenario by speaking the P1 lines into your mic while running the live proactive agent. You can play P2/P3 yourself or have a friend help.
evaluation_criteria: trigger_timing: Did the agent trigger at the right moment (not too early, not too late)?
trigger_precision: Did the agent correctly identify WHY this moment matters?
recommendation_quality: Are the 2 recommendations actionable and non-generic?
recommendation_mode: Is the mode (say/know/both) appropriate for the situation?
false_positive_rate: Does the agent stay quiet during non-trigger moments?
urgency_calibration: Is the urgency level appropriate (high for medical/negotiation, low for social)?

scoring.trigger_timing: 1 = wrong moment, 2 = close but off, 3 = perfect timing
scoring.recommendation_quality: 1 = generic/useless, 2 = somewhat helpful, 3 = genuinely would have helped
scoring.overall_useful: binary — would you have wanted this recommendation in real life?
